title: Sources
text:
The data for this project comes from the World Bank’s World Development Indicators (WDI), accessed using the WDI R package.
The project uses three indicators:

GDP in current US dollars: NY.GDP.MKTP.CD
Trade openness as a percentage of GDP: NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS
Revenue, excluding grants (% of GDP): GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS

Data is retrieved for SAARC member countries:

Afghanistan
Bangladesh
Bhutan
India
Maldives
Nepal
Pakistan
Sri Lanka

Coverage spans annual observations from 2000 to 2024.
Cleaning steps include:

renaming indicators into analysis-friendly variable names
filtering out observations with missing values in the core variables
retaining a consistent regional sample for comparison across time

title: About
text:
I am Faran Abbas, a graduate student in World Economy at Shandong University. You can view my work on GitHub or contact me at faranabbas@hotmail.com.
This project studies fiscal revenue capacity, trade openness, and GDP across SAARC countries from 2000 to 2024 using World Bank World Development Indicators. It is a regional macroeconomic analysis focused on how policy-related indicators differ across South Asian economies. You can view the repository here.
This project was developed as part of Kane’s Data Science Bootcamp.

Summary
This project compares fiscal revenue capacity, trade openness, and GDP across SAARC economies from 2000 to 2024 using World Bank World Development Indicators.
The analysis focuses on Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Using the WDI API in R, the project retrieves and cleans regional macroeconomic data, then visualizes how trade openness relates to GDP across countries and years.
The current chart highlights a positive association between trade openness and GDP, especially for larger and more integrated economies in the region. Revenue excluding grants is included as a core fiscal-capacity variable to support broader comparisons of macroeconomic conditions across SAARC countries.
